title: Nonconvex–strongly concave optimization with a bundled full-Hessian interface.

description_paragraphs:
$$
\min_x\Phi(x),\quad\Phi(x)=\max_y f(x,y).
$$

assumptions.description:
On the declared function domain, $\|
abla f(z)-
abla f(w)\|\le eta\|z-w\|$. The vector $
abla f$ includes both blocks $x,y$.
For each fixed $x$, $-f(x,\cdot)$ is $\mu_y$-strongly convex, uniformly in $x$.

assumptions.scope: Public initial point; the objective-gap or distance term refers to the same solution or value function explicitly specified in this entry

assumptions.description: Neither $x\mapsto f(x,y)$ nor the optimal-value function $\Phi$ is additionally assumed convex.

model.parameter_domain_description: $\Delta$: positive real; $R_y$: nonnegative real; $\beta$: positive real; $d$: integer at least 2; $\varepsilon$: positive real; $\mu_y$: $0<\mu_y\le\beta$; $\rho$: positive real. Derived quantities are defined in the parameter table. Each region states any additional accuracy and dimension conditions.
description_paragraphs: $f:\mathbb{R}^{d_x}\times\mathbb{R}^{d_y}\to\mathbb{R}$, with both blocks unconstrained and Euclidean norms throughout. The joint gradient satisfies $\|\nabla f(z)-\nabla f(w)\|_2\le \beta\|z-w\|_2$.
The condition $f\in C^2$ holds, and the full joint Hessian satisfies $\|\nabla^2f(z)-\nabla^2f(w)\|_{\rm op}\le\rho\|z-w\|_2$.

For every $x$, $f(x,\cdot)$ is uniformly $\mu_y$-strongly concave. Thus $y^\star(x)=\arg\max_y f(x,y)$ is unique and $\Phi(x)=f(x,y^\star(x))$ is differentiable. Neither $f(\cdot,y)$ nor $\Phi$ is assumed convex.
Assume $\inf_x\Phi(x)>-\infty$, with an initial point satisfying $\Phi(x_0)-\inf_x\Phi(x)\le\Delta$.
The public initial point additionally satisfies $\|y_0-y^\star(x_0)\|_2\le R_y$. The condition number is $\kappa=\beta/\mu_y$.

operations.order_convention: Derivative order refers to the scalar payoff $f$. The joint gradient has two blocks; the response signature specifies whether a Hessian or complete derivative jet is supplied.

feedback_quality.description: Exact responses from the same hidden object fixed before interaction

operations.coupling: Deterministic exact responses with repeated queries allowed; stochastic sample-reuse permissions are irrelevant.

public_inputs: Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $\Delta$, $R_y$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, $\mu_y$, $\rho$, together with the stated initial point and feasible geometry. The analytic representation of the hidden function, operator, or matrix is not revealed.
description_paragraphs: Public inputs include block dimensions $d_x,d_y$ and $\Delta$, $R_y$, $\beta$, $\varepsilon$, $\mu_y$, $\rho$, together with the stated initial point and feasible geometry. The analytic representation of the hidden function, operator, or matrix is not revealed.

$$
z\in\mathbb{R}^{d_x+d_y}\longmapsto(f(z),\nabla f(z),\nabla^2f(z)).
$$
One exact call returns the complete joint Hessian, function value, and joint gradient.
Inner optimizers, reduced gradients, and reduced Hessians are not supplied directly. Linear algebra on returned data does not reveal new information about hidden functions.

output.feasibility: Return only the primal block $\widehat x\in X$. An optimal inner point is not required.
output.allowed_postprocessing: arbitrary measurable postprocessing; unqueried output permitted unless restriction says otherwise
description_paragraphs: Return $\widehat x\in\mathbb R^{d_x}$.

The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

metric.finiteness_conditions: compact domain and continuous data, or the specific coercivity/existence promise stated in MODEL
description_paragraphs:
$$
\|\nabla\Phi(\widehat{x})\|_2
$$
The reduced gradient is $\nabla\Phi(x)=\nabla_xf(x,y^\star(x))$. Second-order stationarity is not the target.

objects.definition: Unknown real-valued payoff function $f:\mathbb R^{d_x}\times\mathbb R^{d_y}\to\mathbb R$.
$\Phi(x)=\max_{y\in\mathbb R^{d_y}}f(x,y)$. Strong concavity gives a unique inner optimizer $y^*(x)$, but neither its location nor its value is supplied for free by the oracle.

norms.definition: The Euclidean norm and inner product are $\|v\|_2=(\sum_jv_j^2)^{1/2}$ and $\langle u,v\rangle=\sum_j u_jv_j$. On the joint space use $\|(x,y)\|_2=(\|x\|_2^2+\|y\|_2^2)^{1/2}$. Matrix norms are the induced spectral norms.

notes: The upper bound includes the one-time initialization cost $I_0$. The lower bound holds even under exact dual initialization $R_y=0$. Each of the three comparisons closes only where its leading term dominates $I_0+1$.
evidence.statement_summary: Bundled (f,gradient,full Hessian), L-gradient and rho-Hessian smooth NC-SC; three r-regimes.
evidence.applicability_review: All finite dimensions; arbitrary randomized output with fixed cap and success2/3. Initial gap Delta and dual distance R_y. r=rho*kappa^(3/2)*epsilon/L^2. Lower assumes A1=LDelta/epsilon^2>=C and already R_y=0. Near-matching phase rates require leading term >= I0+1; otherwise retain initialization. FOSP of Phi, not SOSP or HVP cost.
